context:
Core execution-variant guardrails (added 2026-10-09; ADR docs/development/adr/adr-core-execution-variants.md, plan item core-exec-execution-variants):
- Do not register bare generic option keys (engine, mode, backend, runtime, executor, warehouse); the vocabulary parity test fails on them.
- Tinybird is a native platform, not a gateway: do not declare it through the gateways capability. Its dual path (REST ingest, ClickHouse HTTP query) is an adapter detail, not an execution engine.
- Workspace is a namespace, not a compute resource; do not map it to compute_resource unless the ADR says otherwise.
- Results must be distinguishable from native ClickHouse through the platform key and variant_id (core-exec-explorer-variant-identity); never share an identity with clickhouse.
- Follow the execution-variant section of docs/development/new-platform-acceptance-checklist.md.

Revalidated 2026-11-11: still required, still gated on ch-tinybird-spike (open); no Tinybird code exists on origin/develop. Guardrail updates: core-exec-execution-variants, core-exec-explorer-variant-identity and core-exec-compute-resource-unification are done, so those constraints are enforceable now (benchbox/core/execution_engine.py, benchbox/core/compute_resource.py). The referenced docs (docs/development/new-platform-acceptance-checklist.md, adr/adr-core-execution-variants.md, adding-new-platforms.md) now live in the benchbox-site repo, not in docs/ here. In-repo check: `make platform-manifest-check`.
description:
Add BenchBox support for Tinybird as a native platform with its own `tinybird` key (not a gateway). Tinybird requires a dual-path adapter: schema/load go through the Data Source REST API (token auth, .tbl conversion, import-job polling) while queries go through the read-only ClickHouse HTTP interface.

Scope boundary: workspace-database prefixing, token scope requirements documented, no system-table parity claims, throughput streams only if the spike proves session independence. Docs must state the dual-path model and why Tinybird numbers are never comparable to native ClickHouse runs (different storage/ingest path, server-side materializations).

DECISION GATE: proceeds only after ch-tinybird-spike records go on all four unknowns (query path, ingest path, schema translation, namespace reality). A no-go defers this item with the spike evidence as the record.

Guardrails: manifest authority respected; lazy optional imports; compat-docs-check green; tokens in env only; read-only interface failures surfaced cleanly, never as false-success results.
